content.text:
I identify OsO4 (mp-551905) as the single phase present.

- **Single-phase fits:** OsO4 is the only candidate that accounts for the main peaks at about 21.0°, 22.8°, 23.3° and 27.7°, with an R-factor of 0.65. The other eight candidates all leave R-factors of about 0.97–0.99, so they explain almost nothing.
- **What's left after OsO4:** the residual mostly shows paired positive and negative lobes centred on OsO4's own peaks. That pattern suggests a mismatch in peak width or position, such as strain the isotropic model can't capture, rather than a second phase.
- **Caveat:** an R-factor of 0.65 is still poor. I did not run two-phase fits (OsO4 plus another candidate), so a minor second phase isn't strictly ruled out. None of the other candidates fitted the main peaks at all, though, so one seems unlikely.

{"present": ["mp-551905"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "OsO4 is the only candidate matching the main peaks near 21, 22.8, 23.3 and 27.7 degrees; its residual is mostly peak-shape mismatch rather than new peaks, though R=0.65 is poor and no two-phase fit was tried."}
